knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y &=5 \\  -10x-10y &=-25 \\  8x+8y &=20.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & 5 \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & 5 \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-y+\frac{5}{2} \\  y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-y+\frac{5}{2} \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+8y &=18 \\  -4x-16y &=-36 \\  6x+24y &=54.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 8 & 18 \\ -4 & -16 & -36 \\ 6 & 24 & 54\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 8 & 18 \\ -4 & -16 & -36 \\ 6 & 24 & 54\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 4 & 9 \\ -4 & -16 & -36 \\ 6 & 24 & 54\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 4 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & 24 & 54\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 4 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+4y &=9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-4y+9 \\  y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-4y+9 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+z &=1 \\ x+2y+\frac{3}{2}z &=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+\frac{1}{2}z &=\frac{1}{2} \\ y+\frac{1}{2}z &=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-\frac{z}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\ y &=-\frac{z}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{z}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{z}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-\frac{5}{2}z &=-\frac{1}{2} \\ x+2y-\frac{11}{2}z &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 1 & 2 & -\frac{11}{2} & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 1 & 2 & -\frac{11}{2} & -1\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+\frac{1}{2}z &=0 \\ y-3z &=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-\frac{z}{2} \\ y &=3z-\frac{1}{2} \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{z}{2} \\ 3z-\frac{1}{2} \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
